lessons.title: Test-time computation
lessons.description: Evaluate test-time compute, verification and tradeoffs.
lessons.conceptOverview: Reasoning systems spend inference compute on intermediate computation, alternative candidates or search. Self-consistency aggregates multiple solutions; verification checks candidates using rules, tools or learned judges. Hidden internal reasoning need not be exposed to evaluate an answer; request concise explanations and inspect observable evidence.

lessons.title: Supervision, tools & search
lessons.description: Evaluate test-time compute, verification and tradeoffs.
lessons.conceptOverview: Outcome supervision scores final results; process supervision evaluates intermediate steps. Code execution and symbolic tools can verify calculations, but tools need bounded execution and validated inputs. Search helps only when candidate generation and evaluation are useful; a biased verifier can confidently select wrong answers.

lessons.title: Reasoning evaluation & routing
lessons.description: Evaluate test-time compute, verification and tradeoffs.
lessons.conceptOverview: Evaluate accuracy under a fixed latency and cost budget. Include easy tasks where extra reasoning may increase delay or introduce errors. Route requests using task complexity and measured performance, with a fallback when uncertainty is high. Avoid benchmarks contaminated by training examples.

sections.content: Plot task success versus total inference budget for factual lookup and multi-step problems. Choose a routing threshold from measurements rather than model reputation.
